newsitem.title: USA: Audit says 17 Fla. localities in fiscal emergency.
newsitem.headline: Audit says 17 Fla. localities in fiscal emergency.

text.p: Seventeen Florida municipalities and service districts are facing a financial emergency, and 25 others have potential fiscal problems, state Auditor General Charles Lester said in a letter to Gov. Lawton Chiles.
The "financial emergency" list includes those posting deficits for two consecutive years, and is based on a review of 1995 financial statements.
Most Florida municipalities ended their fiscal years Sept 30 and have not completed 1996 audits.

The "potentially troubled" list includes those where further review was needed to determine whether they had adequate resources to cover deficits in their retained earnings or unreserved fund balances.

Under Florida law, the governor could order a deficit reduction plan, and in dire cases, he could appoint a financial emergencies board to take over local finances. No Florida government has ever been taken over by and emergencies board.
